reason: The cited evidence confirms that high configurational entropy stabilizes solid-solution phases and that HEA nanoparticles can exhibit well-mixed surfaces and thermal stability up to 1000 K, but it does not provide support for the key premise that ordering enthalpy overcomes entropy at lower temperatures to cause surface segregation, nor for the direct link between surface mixing changes and performance degradation.
premises: Configurational entropy stabilizes a well-mixed surface at high temperatures.
Ordering enthalpy can overcome entropy at lower temperatures, causing surface segregation.
Surface atomic mixing directly mediates overall nanoparticle stability and performance.
A temperature-dependent entropy–enthalpy balance governs surface mixing.
HEA nanoparticles can maintain a single-phase solid solution with well-mixed surfaces.
